songs.title: Zombie
songs.setup_note: Standard tuning (EADGBE). No capo suggested: the four-chord loop uses open Em, C, G and D shapes.
songs.skill_focus: A four-chord loop (Em, C, G, D) with a steady beat and clean changes. The recording's guitar is heavily distorted and the chorus is louder; this app teaches the chord loop, not the guitar sound.

strumming.note: A starting rhythm exercise. The recording may use a different pattern or picking.

patterns.name: Start: steady downstrokes
patterns.description: Strum down on each count. Keep the motion steady and change shape when the chord cue changes.

patterns.name: Next: driving down-ups
patterns.description: Alternate down and up in steady eighth notes, as in a driving rock strum. Begin slowly; keep moving through chord changes.

chart_check.note: Chart main chords Em/G/C/D (with brief maj7 colourings); capo 0 confirmed. Pulse ~83 BPM. Automatic chart sanity check against the well-known progression and published tempo; not a musical review of timing or arrangement.

songs.title: Good Riddance (Time of Your Life)
songs.setup_note: Standard tuning (EADGBE). No capo suggested: open G, C (often played as Cadd9), D and Em shapes.
songs.skill_focus: Slower changes between G, C, D and Em, with a relaxed folk strum. The recording's guitar is picked rather than strummed, so treat the strum as a way to learn the changes first.

strumming.note: A starting rhythm exercise. The recording may use a different pattern or picking.

patterns.name: Start: steady downstrokes
patterns.description: Strum down on each count. Keep the motion steady and change shape when the chord cue changes.

patterns.name: Next: folk strum (D — D U — U D U)
patterns.description: Keep your hand swinging down and up in steady eighth notes. Touch the strings on the arrows and miss them on the dashes. Start slowly, and keep moving through the chord changes.

songs.title: Bad Moon Rising
songs.setup_note: Standard tuning (EADGBE). No capo suggested: open D, A and G shapes. The beat grid is counted in two half-note beats per bar (cut time), so one bar is two cue dots and four counts.
songs.skill_focus: Quick changes between D, A and G in a bouncy rock-and-roll rhythm. The recording is fast (about 180 quarter-note beats a minute), so start with the slower pattern.

strumming.note: A starting rhythm exercise. The recording may use a different pattern or picking.

patterns.name: Start: steady downstrokes
patterns.description: Strum down on each of the four counts in a bar (two cue beats). At this tempo it is quick: if it is too fast, use the slower pattern. Change shape when the chord cue changes.

patterns.name: Slower: counts 1 and 3 only
patterns.description: Strum down on counts 1 and 3 and let the chord ring on 2 and 4. A relaxed way to learn the changes at this tempo; this is a suggested exercise, not a transcription.
